PAPERS.short: Liu CHARLS cohort county PM2.5 solid fuel joint exposure incident stroke 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of PM(2.5) Exposure and Solid Fuel Use With Incident Stroke: Evidence From a Longitudinal Chinese Cohort.
PAPERS.pm: One-year pre-baseline county-level PM2.5 from the China High Air Pollutants (CHAP) dataset; household solid cooking/heating fuel by questionnaire
PAPERS.affil: First Affiliated Hospital of Henan Medical University, China; First Affiliated Hospital of Henan Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: CHARLS, 13,917 adults (mean age 58.9 y), 1,060 incident strokes. High vs low ambient PM2.5: HR 1.25 (1.04-1.51); solid fuel users vs non-users: HR 1.38 (1.18-1.62); multiplicative interaction p=0.022; HR 1.10 (1.05-1.15) per step of an ordinal joint-exposure score. The PM2.5 contrast is categorical and the cut-point and per-unit estimate are not in the abstract. County-level assignment from a satellite-fused product with one pre-baseline year gives every resident of a county the same value, and solid fuel is a one-time self-report with no measured household PM, so the joint category mixes an ecological and a proxy exposure. Relevance: indirect - indoor-outdoor co-exposure is exactly what paired household and ambient low-cost sensors could resolve.

PAPERS.short: Sarigiannis URBANOME nine-city urban living labs exposome wearable sensors interventions 2026
PAPERS.title: URBANOME: an exposome-based framework linking urban interventions to molecular, health, and policy-relevant outcomes.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient and personal exposure monitoring (wearable sensors, smartphone apps) plus agent-based population exposure modelling
PAPERS.endpoint: Annoyance, sleep breathing problems, FVC, metabolomics/transcriptomics
PAPERS.affil: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Greece; Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Greece
PAPERS.n: Horizon 2020 framework run in nine European urban living labs (Aarhus to Thessaloniki) evaluating co-created active-mobility, greening and traffic-calming interventions before and after, with wearable and ambient monitoring, agent-based exposure modelling, spirometry, blood pressure, HRV and omics. Pilot findings are qualitative: self-reported pollution annoyance and sleep-related breathing problems fell, pollution-related FVC differences attenuated in higher-exposure neighbourhoods; a four-metabolite panel separated pre/post samples with AUROC near 1.0, which the authors call likely overoptimistic. No PM concentration change, effect size or CI is reported in the abstract; designs, comparators and follow-up differ by site, and there is no control arm. Relevance: direct for method - an operational template for coupling personal sensors to intervention evaluation.

PAPERS.short: Jeong review automated robotic field-deployable platforms aerosol cytotoxicity analysis 2026
PAPERS.title: Automated small-scale devices and robotic systems for analyzing the cellular impact of ambient aerosol particles.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient aerosol particles sampled onto cell-based assays
PAPERS.affil: KIST Europe, Germany; Delft University of Technology, Netherlands
PAPERS.n: Conceptual review of small, automated and robotic platforms that deliver ambient aerosol to cells for on-site cytotoxicity analysis, with emphasis on mobile and field-deployable systems, biomimetic device design, and the data acquisition and processing needed for a source-to-effect workflow. It reports no new measurements, no comparison of platforms against standard air-liquid-interface exposure, and no performance numbers in the abstract; search strategy and inclusion criteria are not described, so coverage cannot be judged. Relevance: indirect - toxicity-weighted sensing at the node is the logical step beyond mass concentration, and this is a map of the hardware candidates rather than evidence that any of them works in the field.

PAPERS.short: Toor SHoRT-CA smart home indoor air quality time series contextual anomalies dataset 2026
PAPERS.title: SHoRT-CA: Smart home data repository of time series with contextual anomalies.
PAPERS.pm: Multivariate indoor air-quality time series from IoT smart-home sensors (channels not itemised in the abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Labelled contextual anomalies for detection benchmarking
PAPERS.affil: Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norway; Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Norway
PAPERS.n: Open repository of multivariate indoor air-quality time series from one IoT smart home, with human-activity and environmental-interaction records and contextual anomalies deliberately induced by experiments on the sensors, each documented and labelled for anomaly-detection benchmarking. The abstract does not list which pollutants or particle channels are measured, the sensor models, calibration, or record length, and a single dwelling with induced rather than naturally occurring faults limits how far detectors trained here transfer. Relevance: direct for quality control - labelled anomaly sets are scarce, and automated fault flagging is a standing need for unattended low-cost indoor networks, provided a PM channel is present.

PAPERS.short: de Oliveira Sao Paulo State municipality air-quality anomalies COVID-19 restrictions ecological surveillance 2026
PAPERS.title: Municipality-specific air-quality anomalies and exploratory ecological COVID-19 surveillance analyses in São Paulo State during 2020 restrictions
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Crossref deposit with no abstract on the day of entry and none recoverable by title lookup. From the title, the paper derives municipality-specific air-quality anomalies across Sao Paulo State during the 2020 COVID-19 restrictions and runs exploratory ecological analyses against COVID-19 surveillance data. No pollutant list, monitoring network, anomaly baseline, effect estimate or sample size can be stated, and no finding is asserted here. Any ecological pollution-COVID association from this period carries heavy confounding by mobility, testing intensity and season, which the full text will need to address. Relevance: indirect - lockdown anomaly baselines are a reference case for separating emission change from meteorology at municipal scale; recheck for the abstract in the weekly sweep.
